coverage_criterion.reporting: Every exclusion named with its reason in the run file and in any writeup.
coverage_criterion.definition: Coverage is the fraction of TOTAL rubric input weight actually supplied — core and live together, out of 100. This is the definition the pre-registered target_coverage of 0.36 was set against, and it does not change now that the rubric is split. Redefining coverage as "fraction of core weight supplied" would make the pre-registered bar trivial to clear, which is moving the threshold by another name. core_coverage and live_coverage are reported alongside it as diagnostics and are NOT what the criterion tests.
coverage_criterion.exclusion_caveat: Excluding on coverage means excluding on a property that may correlate with outcome. Dropping one project from a 13-project primary comparison is a 7.7% change in sample. Whether exclusions skew by class cannot be checked without opening outcomes, so: the floor is pre-registered blind, exclusions are applied mechanically, and after evaluation the writeup reports the class composition of every excluded project, whatever it shows.

note: Blind run. Scoring code has never read the resolved labels. Git-only features; the rubric's live_tool_only and not_reconstructable inputs are absent and each dimension renormalises over what was available. Dropped dimensions lower max_achievable and are NOT redistributed. PR velocity is substituted with commit velocity at gate 2. Gate 5 (counterparty) is not evaluated for any project. The gates are not tested by this corpus — see runs/README.md.
